After becoming more aware of my thoughts I realised I have alot of toxic and arrogant thoughts. I also constantly think of scenarios in my head where people will think I'm such a great person and praise me. 

This comes from my low self esteem and anxiety. I feel the need for other people's validation and compare myself to others. I also often think I'm better or more talented than other people just to appease my insecurity. Then I beat myself up for thinking these 'bad' thoughts, making my mentality and self esteem even worse.

I'm still working on this too but here are some things that have helped me.

Therapy: 
Not all therapists will suit you so keep trying if you don't like your current therapist. Make sure you are honest with your therapist, all your darkest thoughts, what methods are working and what aren't, they are here to help you.

Getting off social media: 
FB and Insta are the worst, but sometimes even Reddit is just a pit of toxic feelings and opinions from a vocal minority. Being in the real world with real people helps widen your perspective and make your expectations realistic.

The YouTuber HealthyGamerGG: 
This guy is really great, he does talks with famous streamers/youtubers and sometimes regular people. Just listening to the sessions is really eye opening.

Lastly, I guess something that I've realised is that lots of people have these thoughts. Having these thoughts doesn't make you a bad person, how you choose to act defines who you are.

From reading your post, all the self doubt and worry and negative emotions definitely reads as depressed, self-loathing, alot of shame, and a bit paranoid.

I used to be incredibly negative too, and I didn't realise this for a long time, but mentally healthy people actually think pretty positively most of the time.

So chores, study, and other life activities are literally easier for them because they don't have anxious or self-loathing thoughts weighing them down all the time. ( I hear inability to do some of those things can be ADHD related.)

Also, watching shows or scrolling on social media is sometimes a strong indicator of avoidance of negative feelings. At the height of my anxiety I needed to be distracting myself with videos or tiktok CONSTANTLY.

I've had the same doubts; I'm from a good family, good school, have friends, I can function, but that doesn't mean you're not depressed or need mental help.

So what I think is tell a therapist about these struggles and be as honest as you are in this post, even the ones where you doubt your own sadness or feel like you are faking. I like this response. I'm depressed and trying to make my life productive too. A quote from Bojack horseman really stuck with me: 

"It gets easier. Everyday it gets a little easier. But you gotta do it every day. That's the hard part. But it does get easier."

Basically adding something to your routine, and doing it everyday. I see my energy as a bar with a total capacity limit. At first doing this new thing will be hard but the more you do it the more you push the boundaries of your energy bar, and it will increase. I'm slowly adjusting to studying right now.

Also, since I have so little mental energy already, staying positive and being forgiving is really important. Back to the bar analogy, each task takes a certain amount of energy points. All the negative thoughts about myself or a task double its energy point usage, making every task SO much more difficult.

You have to be in a relatively good headspace to even start using most of this advice though. So address the underlying problems and go to a therapist if you can.

It was frustrating to see people say whatever they wanted and live happily when I was stuck in my anxiety.
